What counted in the public test: Reported construction year. For condos this can describe the building that contains the unit.
Direct acquisition: Assessor building summary; join local building/parcel ID and roll year.
Example source mapping: Clark PACS PropBldgSumInfoVw.YrBlt.
Fallback/qualification: Ask for a dated building-characteristics feed if local roll lacks it; distinguish original year from effective age.

What counted in the public test: Explicit effective year from the assessor. Remodel year or last refresh cannot stand in.
Direct acquisition: Assessor improvement schedule only when it explicitly defines effective year.
Example source mapping: Clark taxlots BldgEffYrBlt, separately from BldgYrBlt.
Fallback/qualification: Use a published effective-year field or omit. A renovation permit date cannot substitute.

What counted in the public test: Residential living area for a house or assessed dwelling. Commercial usable area, effective area, and average unit size are separate.
Direct acquisition: Residential assessor/unit schedule with a defined living-area measure.
Example source mapping: Clark PACS building summary LivingArea; D.C. condo LIVING_GBA has a distinct local definition.
Fallback/qualification: Use exact unit plans or licensed structural fields. Keep building gross and residential living area separate.

What counted in the public test: Explicit gross floor area for the subject building or lot. Mixed-definition building area stays separate.
Direct acquisition: Assessor building card or official land-use/assessment roll.
Example source mapping: D.C. residential GBA; NYC PLUTO BldgArea is a lot-level measure.
Fallback/qualification: Acquire building plans or CRE coverage for individual buildings. Validate gross/net and multi-building scope.

What counted in the public test: Explicit first-floor area in the King County residential building extract.
Direct acquisition: Assessor floor or sketch schedule with an explicit first-floor area.
Example source mapping: King County SQFT1STFLOOR is a defined local example.
Fallback/qualification: Request permitted building plans or leave unknown; a footprint alone is inadequate.

What counted in the public test: Numeric story count for the appropriate building or lot. A floor number, “3+,” or unit floor is excluded. NYC reports the tallest building.
Direct acquisition: Building improvement record, including jurisdictional fractional-story rules.
Example source mapping: D.C. residential STORIES; NYC NumFloors is reported at the lot’s PLUTO scope.
Fallback/qualification: Use building inventory or manager plans when missing. Distinguish building stories, unit levels and suite floor.

What counted in the public test: Reported residential bedrooms. Zero counts are included only where the source reports a usable unit-level bedroom value; elsewhere positive-only is conservative.
Direct acquisition: Residential building or condo/unit assessor record.
Example source mapping: D.C. BEDRM in residential and condo layers; Clark Bedrooms.
Fallback/qualification: Use unit-specific manager/owner evidence for rentals. A studio can have zero. Ordinary office profiles omit it.

What counted in the public test: Total from full + 0.5 × half (and + 0.75 × three-quarter in King County) when all components are present. Unspecified integer totals are kept separately.
Direct acquisition: Residential assessor unit schedule with explicit total or documented calculation.
Example source mapping: D.C. BATHRM / HF_BATHRM and Clark FullBaths/HalfBaths/ThrQtrsBaths are components.
Fallback/qualification: Use a residential unit plan where missing. Never guess the total from incomplete parts or treat office fixtures as home baths.

What counted in the public test: Recorded full-bath count, including explicit zeros. Cook warns that its source may default a missing value to one.
Direct acquisition: Assessor or permitted unit plan identifying full bathrooms.
Example source mapping: Clark PACS PropBldgSumInfoVw.FullBaths.
Fallback/qualification: Only use an equivalent local definition; store explicit zero and missing separately.

What counted in the public test: Recorded half baths. With separate three-quarter baths, only credit this row when the three-quarter count is zero; keep both raw quantities.
Direct acquisition: Separate half, quarter, three-quarter or partial fields with their original definitions.
Example source mapping: Clark HalfBaths/ThrQtrsBaths; D.C. HF_BATHRM means half baths.
Fallback/qualification: Keep the component label or document a conversion. No automatic partial-to-total derivation.

What counted in the public test: Reported fireplace count, allowing recorded zero. Cook counts chimney flues externally and is kept separate.
Direct acquisition: Assessor improvement detail identifying count or presence.
Example source mapping: D.C. residential/condo FIREPLACES; Clark building summary Fireplaces.
Fallback/qualification: An authorized unit plan or disclosure can fill gaps. Separate the count, binary presence and common lobby equipment.

What counted in the public test: Recognized architectural style on a dwelling. Construction class and “attached” alone do not establish architectural style.
Direct acquisition: Assessor style code plus the vintage-specific codebook.
Example source mapping: D.C. STYLE_D; Clark BldgStyle.
Fallback/qualification: Limit mapping to documented equivalents; a generic use class does not establish style.

What counted in the public test: Overall condition or an assessor-defined repair condition. Exterior-only and composite condition/desirability/utility are separate.
Direct acquisition: Assessor or inspection rating plus inspection year and source scale.
Example source mapping: D.C. CNDTN_D; Clark Condition.
Fallback/qualification: Current interior condition requires an authorized dated observation; never market a historic grade as current.

What counted in the public test: Published building/construction quality or recognized assessor grade. No estimate from price.
Direct acquisition: Assessor improvement grade; include source scale and vintage.
Example source mapping: D.C. GRADE_D in residential and commercial schedules.
Fallback/qualification: Use licensed rating or reviewed appraisal if needed; distinguish quality from condition.

What counted in the public test: Explicit building count or documented improvement-card count. Unit count and condo PIN count are different.
Direct acquisition: Assessor building identifiers grouped by parcel and observation year; or documented count.
Example source mapping: Clark taxlot BldgCount. D.C. BLDG_NUM is an identifier, not a count.
Fallback/qualification: Deduplicate building IDs rather than counting transfers; distinguish structures, outbuildings and roof detections.

What counted in the public test: Reported exterior-wall material/finish. Building-class text alone does not establish it.
Direct acquisition: Assessor improvement construction table or permitted building specs.
Example source mapping: D.C. EXTWALL_D residential and commercial.
Fallback/qualification: Use a dated shell/building source. Keep unknown/other distinct from a material.

What counted in the public test: Reported roof-cover material. A roof shape is a separate fact.
Direct acquisition: Assessor roof-material field and codebook; permitted roof work where meaningful.
Example source mapping: D.C. ROOF_D; validate its codes describe material, not shape.
Fallback/qualification: Seek a licensed building description or authorized plans if missing. A shared roof belongs on the building.

What counted in the public test: Reported heating type/system including a known code, or explicitly absent when recorded.
Direct acquisition: Assessor mechanical field, permitted retrofit or operator equipment record.
Example source mapping: D.C. HEAT_D; King County HEATSYSTEM.
Fallback/qualification: Keep central plant and in-unit equipment separate. Bind observation to the date and the asset it serves.

What counted in the public test: Reported cooling type, including explicit central air or explicit absence of cooling. “No central A/C” does not rule out other cooling.
Direct acquisition: Assessor cooling field or permitted mechanical plans.
Example source mapping: D.C. AC can indicate availability. A binary Y does not establish central AC.
Fallback/qualification: Named cooling type needs a system-specific record or qualified operator input.

What counted in the public test: Documented garage or recorded absence where semantics are explicit. Unlisted amenities stay unknown.
Direct acquisition: Assessor improvement sketch, condo declaration or recorded parking interest.
Example source mapping: King County distinguishes attached/basement garage areas, which are area fields.
Fallback/qualification: Use descriptive garage type only when explicit. For condos identify deeded vs common garage.

What counted in the public test: Reported attached/basement/detached garage or carport type. Label the recorded type and its scope.
Direct acquisition: Assessor parking improvement codes, building/parking plan or condo declaration.
Example source mapping: Cook County improvement schema is an acquisition lead; validate parking semantics locally.
Fallback/qualification: Request operator or CRE data for structured, surface, assigned or shared parking.

What counted in the public test: Explicit Boston parking count including recorded zero. An assessor count on a condo account does not verify a deeded or assigned space.
Direct acquisition: Assessor parking count when explicitly recorded; recorded allocation/approved plan.
Example source mapping: Test county parking schedules and permitted site plan; no universal count field demonstrated.
Fallback/qualification: Operator/manager evidence is often needed for assignments. Do not convert area to stalls.

What counted in the public test: Measured area of explicitly recorded garage/carport improvements in Dallas. Label it covered parking area. Uncovered capacity stays unknown.
Direct acquisition: Assessor garage/sketch areas with the garage subtype and measured extent.
Example source mapping: King County SQFTGARATCH and SQFTGARBSMT distinguish garage areas.
Fallback/qualification: Do not use garage area as whole-site parking area. Request site plans for surface parking or complex-wide totals.

What counted in the public test: Source lot acres, or accepted lot square feet divided by 43,560. Shared condo land is excluded.
Direct acquisition: Assessor recorded acreage, recorded plat, or a separately labeled geometric computation.
Example source mapping: Clark AssrAc vs GISAc; validate parcel status and area units.
Fallback/qualification: For condos/rentals show parent area unless a separate legal lot is documented.

What counted in the public test: Source lot square feet, or documented acres × 43,560. The two lot displays often share one measurement.
Direct acquisition: Same legal lot as above; preserve original area source and unit.
Example source mapping: Clark AssrSqFt vs GISSqft; D.C. LANDAREA.
Fallback/qualification: Permit an exact unit conversion for the same measured area. Do not confuse parcel area and living area.

What counted in the public test: Explicit platted lot number. NYC’s tax-lot number remains a separate identifier.
Direct acquisition: Recorder subdivision plat, assessor legal lot designation.
Example source mapping: NYC tax lots use local block/lot conventions; a tax lot number is not necessarily a platted lot.
Fallback/qualification: Use a permitted plat or recorded lot designation; never substitute an APN or apartment number.

What counted in the public test: Recorded property/site address. Exact unit match requires its own test. A recovered parcel address alone does not prove unit lookup.
Direct acquisition: Assessor situs/site address or local addressing authority; national NAD for discovery.
Example source mapping: Clark Situs* / situs point records; King SITUSADDRESS.
Fallback/qualification: Preserve unit input and spelling. Postal mailing/contact address is a separate attribute.

What counted in the public test: Published nine-digit situs ZIP, excluding 0000 suffixes. Measures recorded postal extension only, without mail deliverability validation.
Direct acquisition: Retain a lawfully reusable explicit ZIP+4 for its exact delivery destination when terms allow.
Example source mapping: USPS ZIP+4 reference service is the authority; county/owner ZIP5 cannot supply the suffix.
Fallback/qualification: Reuse an already licensed check under its terms, contract postal processing, or omit. Range file alone does not validate delivery or residency.

What counted in the public test: Jurisdiction-scoped APN, PIN, BBL, property ID or assessment account. Store its namespace and any leading zero.
Direct acquisition: Assessor/recorder parcel ID or tax-account crosswalk, including jurisdiction and date.
Example source mapping: D.C. SSL and NYC BBL are local identifiers. Clark Prop_id/LandProp_id require a validated relationship.
Fallback/qualification: Retain source ID and leading zeros. An internal tax account ID must be labeled accordingly; require a unit crosswalk for stacked condos.

What counted in the public test: Explicit source jurisdiction or verified geographic crosswalk.
Direct acquisition: Census TIGER county/equivalent plus situs spatial join.
Example source mapping: Census county names are keyed by GEOID; check boundaries and situs county, not postal city.
Fallback/qualification: No paid feed required for the geography. Boundary or jurisdiction ambiguity requires review.

What counted in the public test: Verified government county FIPS inferred from the jurisdiction or municipality/borough crosswalk. A local tax code is a different ID.
Direct acquisition: Census county/equivalent geographic codes.
Example source mapping: 2026 Census County Adjacency file supplies five-character GEOIDs.
Fallback/qualification: Preserve leading zeros and vintage; map local tax authority separately.

What counted in the public test: City jurisdiction from a spatial or tax district join, or city-wide assessment scope. A mailing city alone does not establish municipality.
Direct acquisition: Government boundaries / incorporated-place data or an authoritative assessor municipality field.
Example source mapping: TIGER/Line places and county subdivisions have different legal/statistical meanings.
Fallback/qualification: Report unincorporated where appropriate. A census-designated place or mailing city does not establish incorporation.

What counted in the public test: King County’s recorded plat name, excluding generic/unplatted labels. Display as a recorded subdivision/plat.
Direct acquisition: Recorded plat/subdivision field or local assessor index.
Example source mapping: Clark PlatName / PlatCode.
Fallback/qualification: Do not equate neighborhood names, HOA marketing, or postal localities with a legal subdivision.

What counted in the public test: Reported tax area, taxing-authority-group or levy code, qualified by jurisdiction.
Direct acquisition: Local assessor/tax district codebook and roll-year account.
Example source mapping: Clark TaxCode; confirm its year and district meaning.
Fallback/qualification: Keep each custodian’s code system. State/county FIPS alone cannot produce a local tax-area code.

What counted in the public test: Normalized property type from the publisher’s classes, codes or documented building form.
Direct acquisition: Assessor property/land-use class and CAMA family, normalized with a versioned crosswalk.
Example source mapping: D.C. separate residential, condominium and commercial layers; each has USECODE.
Fallback/qualification: Store building type separately from legal tenure or occupancy. Permit mixed classification.

What counted in the public test: Published assessor class or broader class decoded from its published use code. Preserve the publisher’s vocabulary.
Direct acquisition: County assessor use/class dictionary plus original code.
Example source mapping: Cook assessor improvement classes; D.C. published use codes.
Fallback/qualification: Preserve local code and normalized grouping. Require source provenance for any vendor-specific taxonomy.

What counted in the public test: An additional, specific official subclass, e.g. medical office. Excludes generic or missing subclasses.
Direct acquisition: Detailed assessor/use code and legal-interest classification where available.
Example source mapping: Cook County class dictionary is an example of a local codebook.
Fallback/qualification: Keep source labels or show a less specific type. Subtype conventions are not nationally uniform.

What counted in the public test: Assessment use from the local or statewide use classification. Store separately from legal zoning.
Direct acquisition: Local land-use record, assessor use code or verified parcel GIS classification.
Example source mapping: NYC PLUTO LandUse; Clark PropertyUseClass.
Fallback/qualification: Distinguish present use, mixed use, zoning and legally permitted future use.

What counted in the public test: Local assessment/building-use code. Florida credits its optional county PA_UC independently of statewide DOR_UC.
Direct acquisition: Raw local assessor code, county and year before mapping.
Example source mapping: D.C. USECODE and Clark PropertyUseClass are jurisdiction-specific.
Fallback/qualification: Never interpret a number using another county’s codebook.

What counted in the public test: Boston’s affirmative owner-occupancy flag on residential accounts. A negative flag establishes neither tenant occupancy nor vacancy.
Direct acquisition: Only an explicit permitted assessor occupancy indicator or separately labeled, consented confirmation.
Example source mapping: A homestead exemption or matching mailing/situs address is different evidence.
Fallback/qualification: Do not infer a named occupant or grant access. Commercial leasing occupancy and vacancy are separate metrics.

What counted in the public test: Reported parcel or abbreviated tax-roll legal description. Display its scope and source. A tax-roll excerpt is not the deed.
Direct acquisition: Assessor legal-description field or official recorder/plat extract for this interest.
Example source mapping: Clark LegalShort and PACS legal files; use the correct condo estate or parent land.
Fallback/qualification: Use a permitted document or licensed recorder source if needed. Respect redaction and avoid claiming a legal title opinion.

What counted in the public test: Vendor-issued identifier. Public parcel IDs can serve the application separately.
Direct acquisition: No public creator of the ATTOM ID field. Issue an immutable Pantopus ID.
Example source mapping: Use jurisdiction + APN/BBL/SSL and internal building/unit links for independent identity.
Fallback/qualification: Under a no-ATTOM plan, replace the row with Pantopus/source ID. Preserve legacy crosswalks only if written rights allow.

What counted in the public test: Vendor model output. An independently published tax assessment has different meaning.
Direct acquisition: Public assessments or closed sales can be inputs; their recorded values have separate labels.
Example source mapping: RentCast documents an estimate; ATTOM’s residential model scope is limited.
Fallback/qualification: Qualify a residential model per class. For whole apartment/office assets, use commercial comps, normalized NOI/cap-rate model or reviewed appraisal. Withhold an unsupported value.

What counted in the public test: A range from a valuation model or licensed source.
Direct acquisition: No authoritative nationwide public model interval.
Example source mapping: RentCast documents priceRangeLow/priceRangeHigh.
Fallback/qualification: Return low/high from the same vetted model/date, or calibrate held-out residual intervals per market/type; otherwise omit.

What counted in the public test: A documented and calibrated model confidence metric.
Direct acquisition: No public counterpart for ATTOM’s score.
Example source mapping: Comparable correlation is not an overall estimate-confidence score.
Fallback/qualification: Require documented scale and calibration; with zero model spend show unavailable until a Pantopus score is independently validated.

What counted in the public test: Date of the particular model run, distinct from assessment year, sale date and import date.
Direct acquisition: Use the matched model valuation’s as-of date, not the assessor snapshot.
Example source mapping: An API fetch date or latest comparable sale cannot stand in for model vintage.
Fallback/qualification: Require an explicit source date, or separate ‘retrieved on’ from ‘valued on’. Hide the stale/unknown date when rights or accuracy require it.
